The current account balance is expected to slightly widen to about 1 percent of GDP in 2022–23.","locator":"page 13","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"IMF staff projections for 2022-2023","source_limitations":["Staff projections subject to economic assumptions; downside risks noted"],"question_ids":["5B.9","5B.10"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0012","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Mexico's minimum wage rose from 42 percent of the median formal sector wage in 2018 to a projected 59 percent in 2022, and real per capita labor income increased approximately 5 percent year-over-year by mid-2022.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Mexican government","action":"raised minimum wage and implemented labor market measures","mechanism":"minimum wage policy; economic recovery and remittances","outcome":"Minimum wage projected to reach 59% of median formal wage by 2022 vs 42% in 2018; real per capita labor income up ~5% y/y by mid-2022","dates":["2018","2022","mid-2022"],"quantities":["42 percent to 59 percent of median formal wage","~5 percent y/y real per capita labor income increase"],"excerpt":"The administration has increased the universal social pensions and is projected to raise the minimum wage from 42 percent of the median formal sector wage in 2018 to 59 percent in 2022. Overall, these fiscal efforts, the higher minimum wage, and other labor market measures may have contributed to an increase in real per capita labor income of about 5 percent (y/y) by mid-2022.","locator":"page 19","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"Labor market outcomes 2018-2022","source_limitations":["Staff estimation of causal contribution; remittances also contributed"],"question_ids":["5B.8"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0013","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"IMF staff simulation of a three-layer downside shock (oil/food price shock, inflation expectations dislocation with sharper rate increases, and 1 percent domestic demand decline) showed cumulative output losses exceeding 2 percent below baseline at the trough.","claim_type":"interpretation","polarity":"adverse","actor":"IMF staff","action":"simulated three-layer downside scenario using G20MOD model","mechanism":"(1) oil/food price shock +10%/+50%; (2) inflation expectations dislocation causing sharper domestic rate increases and output falling >1% below baseline by H1 2023; (3) 1% domestic demand decline","outcome":"Cumulative output loss >2% below baseline at trough; headline inflation ~1% above elevated baseline; substantial cumulative pressure on corporate interest rates","dates":[],"quantities":["+10 percent oil price shock","+50 percent food price shock",">1 percent output decline H1 2023",">2 percent output below baseline at trough"],"excerpt":"In a second layer, output levels fall substantially below baseline, peaking at more than 1 percent below in the first half of 2023. Last, a third layer added with a 1 percent decline in domestic demand brings output to more than 2 percent below baseline at the trough.","locator":"page 16","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"Scenario analysis for 2022-2023 downside risks","source_limitations":["Model simulation; does not model capital flow shock directly; illustrative scenario not baseline forecast"],"question_ids":["5B.9"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0014","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Banxico has published updated inflation forecasts with every rate decision since August 2021 and provided rate guidance in monetary policy statements to help the public understand policy decisions.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Banxico","action":"improved monetary policy communication","mechanism":"publication of updated inflation forecasts since August 2021; rate guidance in monetary policy statements","outcome":"Public better able to understand Governing Board's policy decisions; staff recommends further publishing of expected policy rate path","dates":["August 2021"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Banxico has appropriately taken steps to help the public better understand its policy decisions in this context. Steps have included the publication of updated inflation forecasts with every rate decision since August 2021 and, more recently, guidance on the direction of the next policy rate change in the monetary policy statement.","locator":"page 18","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"Banxico communication improvements 2021-2022","source_limitations":["Communication effectiveness not independently measured"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0015","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Philips curve estimates for Mexico confirm backward-looking elements in the domestic inflation process, creating additional risks from recent inflation shocks and asymmetric upside risks in the one-to-two-year monetary policy horizon.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"adverse","actor":"IMF staff","action":"estimated Philips curve relationships for Mexico","mechanism":"Philips curve analysis showing backward-looking inflation dynamics","outcome":"Backward-looking elements confirmed; upside inflation risks more likely than downside; risk management approach calls for policy rates to rise further and stay firmly restrictive; real ex ante rate to peak >5% in 2023","dates":[],"quantities":["over 5 percent real ex ante policy rate peak in 2023"],"excerpt":"One contributing factor is backward-looking elements in the inflation process in Mexico according to Philips curve estimates for Mexico, which suggests additional risks from recent inflation shocks. Given these asymmetric risks and the substantial costs of de-anchoring wage and price formation, a risk management approach would argue for policy rates to rise further and stay firmly restrictive for some time.","locator":"page 18","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"Analysis of inflation dynamics 2022","source_limitations":["Model-based estimates; Philips curve relationships subject to specification uncertainty"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0016","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"The Mexican authorities agreed that the current conjuncture presented elevated uncertainty with risks tilted to the downside, with the budget central estimate at 2.1 percent growth for 2023 while Banxico forecast 1.6 percent.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"context","actor":"Mexican authorities and Banxico","action":"acknowledged downside risks to growth outlook","mechanism":"elevated uncertainty from global and domestic interest rates, high inflation, U.S. growth slowdown","outcome":"Risks tilted to downside; budget central estimate 2.1% growth 2023; Banxico forecast 1.6%; U.S. slowdown identified as headline risk","dates":[],"quantities":["2.1 percent budget central estimate","1.6 percent Banxico forecast","0.8 to 2.4 percent Banxico forecast range"],"excerpt":"The authorities agreed that the current conjuncture of high and rising global and domestic interest rates, high inflation, and downside risks to growth presented elevated uncertainty with risks tilted to the downside. The budget contemplates growth for 2023 in the range of 1.2 to 3.0 percent in 2023, with a central estimate of 2.1, while the latest Banxico forecast puts it between 0.8 and 2.4 percent with a central estimate of 1.6 percent.","locator":"page 15","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"Authorities' assessment of 2023 outlook","source_limitations":["Range of forecasts reflects uncertainty; estimates subject to revision"],"question_ids":["5B.9"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0017","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Mexico's fuel price stabilization policy disproportionately benefited higher income households, with the top 20 percent of the income distribution accounting for about 45 percent of fuel excise tax collection while the bottom 20 percent accounted for 6 percent.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"adverse","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"implemented fuel price stabilization with disproportionate distributional impact","mechanism":"retail fuel price stabilization; top-to-bottom income distribution analysis of fuel tax collection","outcome":"Top 20% income received ~45% of fuel excise tax collection; bottom 20% received 6%; measure disproportionately benefited higher income households","dates":[],"quantities":["top 20 percent received 45 percent of fuel excise tax collection","bottom 20 percent received 6 percent"],"excerpt":"The measure has come at a sizeable budgetary cost, estimated at around 1.5 percent of GDP, and has disproportionately benefited higher income households. Using 2020 data, the authorities estimate that the top 20 percent of the income distribution accounted for about 45 percent of the fuel excise tax collection whereas the bottom 20 percent accounted for 6 percent.","locator":"page 19","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010 (citing Mexican Ministry of Finance data)","period_fit":"Distributional analysis based on 2020 data","source_limitations":["2020 data; fuel tax collection not equivalent to fuel subsidy incidence; analysis by authorities"],"question_ids":["5B.8"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0018","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"The Mexican fiscal framework's balanced budget rule and debt issuance constraints limit the scope for countercyclical fiscal policy, constraining the ability to provide targeted support in the event of a negative shock.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"adverse","actor":"Mexican fiscal framework","action":"maintains balanced budget rule and debt issuance constraints","mechanism":"balanced budget rule and debt issuance limits","outcome":"Scope for countercyclical fiscal policy is limited; only modest steps possible to increase ability to provide targeted support in a negative shock","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Under Mexico's fiscal framework—which includes both a balanced budget rule and constraints on debt issuance—the scope to pursue a countercyclical fiscal policy is limited. Modest steps could, however, increase the ability of fiscal policy to provide targeted support in the event of a negative shock.","locator":"page 20","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"Structural fiscal framework assessment","source_limitations":["Structural constraint assessment; modest reform options identified by staff"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0019","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"The 2023 budget entailed no change in the tax code but highlighted continued efforts to reduce tax evasion and avoidance, with authorities projecting oil prices well below 2022 levels and expected improvement in excise collections.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"context","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"maintained tax code unchanged while continuing anti-evasion efforts","mechanism":"no tax code changes; continued anti-evasion and avoidance efforts","outcome":"Tax code unchanged; anti-evasion efforts ongoing; oil price assumptions below 2022 levels; excise collections expected to improve","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"On the revenue side, the budget entails no change in the tax code but highlights continued efforts to reduce tax evasion and avoidance. The authorities project oil price to be well below 2022 levels, and excise collections are expected to improve.","locator":"page 13","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"2023 revenue policy","source_limitations":["Anti-evasion effectiveness not independently quantified; oil price projections subject to uncertainty"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0020","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Headline and core inflation were projected to return to the midpoint of the target band in mid-2024, with inflation expected to plateau at around 8.5 percent in H2 2022, and risks to the inflation outlook judged tilted to the upside.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"context","actor":"IMF staff","action":"projected inflation path and balance of risks","mechanism":"inflation trajectory modeling; balance of risks assessment","outcome":"Inflation plateau ~8.5% H2 2022; return to target band midpoint by mid-2024 assuming policy rate ~10% by early 2023; upside risks to inflation outlook","dates":[],"quantities":["~8.5 percent H2 2022 plateau","mid-2024 target band midpoint return"],"excerpt":"Inflation is projected to plateau at around 8½ percent in the second half of 2022 and then decline gradually. Core and headline inflation are expected to return to the midpoint of the target band in mid-2024. On balance, risks to this inflation outlook are judged to be tilted to the upside.","locator":"page 14","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"Staff inflation projections 2022-2024","source_limitations":["Conditional on policy rate path and assumptions; upside risks acknowledged"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0021","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Interest rates on peso-denominated Mexican securities reached their highest levels since the Global Financial Crisis, with the yield on 1-year government bonds rising by more than 250 basis points, and real yields on inflation-linked Udibonos rising by 80 basis points.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"adverse","actor":"Mexican financial markets","action":"interest rates rose significantly","mechanism":"tightening of financial conditions; rising yields on peso-denominated securities","outcome":"Interest rates on peso securities at highest since Global Financial Crisis; 1-year government bond yield rose >250 bps; real Udibono yield up 80 bps","dates":[],"quantities":[">250 basis points yield increase on 1-year government bond","80 basis points real yield increase on Udibonos"],"excerpt":"Interest rates on peso-denominated Mexican securities are at their highest since the Global Financial Crisis. The yield on a 20-year bond has risen by more than 250 basis points for a 20-year bond. The real yield on an inflation linked Udibono maturing in 2031 has risen by 80 bps.","locator":"page 11","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"Financial conditions assessment 2022","source_limitations":["Market data; period comparison relative to Global Financial Crisis"],"question_ids":["5B.3"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0022","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"The peso remained broadly stable against the U.S. dollar despite moderate portfolio outflows, supported by a rising interest rate differential, fiscal discipline, monetary policy commitment to price stability, and solid remittance inflows.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Mexican economy / Banxico","action":"maintained peso stability despite portfolio outflows","mechanism":"rising interest rate differential; fiscal discipline; monetary policy commitment to price stability; remittance inflows","outcome":"Peso broadly stable against USD; outflows offset by strong buying from domestic institutional investors, notably pension funds","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"The peso has remained broadly stable. The outflows were offset by strong buying by domestic institutional investors, notably pension funds. The peso has remained stable against the U.S. dollar, supported by a rising interest rate differential compared to the U.S., relatively strong fiscal fundamentals, monetary policy commitment to price stability, and solid remittance inflows.","locator":"page 11","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"Balance of payments assessment 2022","source_limitations":["Remittances self-reported; domestic institutional investor data subject to reporting lags"],"question_ids":["5B.3"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0023","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"IMF staff recommended that Banxico publish more information on the policy rate path underlying its macro forecast, including the expected peak rate and triggers for changes, and conduct a broader review of its inflation targeting framework experience for further improvements.","claim_type":"recommendation","polarity":"context","actor":"IMF staff","action":"recommended improvements to Banxico communication and framework","mechanism":"enhanced publication of policy rate path expectations; broader inflation targeting framework review","outcome":"Recommendations: publish expected peak rate and length of stay at peak; possible triggers for policy changes; broader review of inflation targeting framework for further improvements","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"To further strengthen this understanding, Banxico could begin publishing more information on the policy rate path that underpins its macro forecast, including the expected rate and length of its stay at the peak of the tightening cycle, and possible triggers for changes in policies. A broader review of the experience with Banxico's inflation targeting framework over the past two decades could provide useful suggestions for further improvements to the policy framework and the communications toolkit.","locator":"page 18","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"Framework improvement recommendations","source_limitations":["Recommendations not yet implemented; framework review not yet conducted"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0024","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Staff recommended that changing the retail fuel price regime to more market-based pricing could create room for more targeted fiscal support, allow passthrough of global fuel prices, encourage transition to greener energy, and reduce budgetary subsidy costs.","claim_type":"recommendation","polarity":"context","actor":"IMF staff","action":"recommended market-based reform of fuel pricing regime","mechanism":"more market-based fuel pricing allowing passthrough of global prices","outcome":"Could allow passthrough of global fuel prices to domestic retail prices; encourage transition to greener sources; reduce budgetary cost of subsidies; strengthen price signals; allow fiscal savings to be partially reinvested in targeted support for vulnerable households","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Changing the retail fuel price regime could create room for more targeted support in case of a prolonged global oil price increase. More market-based fuel pricing could allow for a passthrough of global fuel prices to domestic retail prices, encourage transition to greener sources of energy, and reduce the budgetary cost of subsidies.","locator":"page 20","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010","period_fit":"Structural fiscal policy recommendation","source_limitations":["Staff recommendation; not yet adopted by authorities; political economy constraints acknowledged"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.6","5B.9"],"verification_status":"pending","premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0025","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"The Mexican authorities emphasized that fuel price stabilization had been central to supporting households and restraining inflation, aligned with the President's commitment, and that the pricing mechanism had dampening second-round inflation effects, though the main goal was to support underserved agricultural communities.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"mixed","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":"defended fuel price stabilization policy","mechanism":"retail fuel price stabilization; President's commitment","outcome":"Fuel stabilization central to household support and inflation restraint; pricing mechanism said to dampen second-round inflation effects; main policy goal was to support underserved agricultural communities with positive expected effects on yields","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"The authorities emphasized that, despite these measures, they sustained momentum on the administration's flagship reforms. Fuel price stabilization in particular had been central to efforts to support households and restrain inflation, in line with the President's commitment to the people. They highlighted analysis suggesting that, in addition to supporting households, the pricing mechanism has dampening second-round inflation effects.
